core_obligations: Record that the outer data is Tor independent, introduce the right adjoints a, b, c and the three arrows gamma_{top}, gamma_{bot}, gamma_{rect}, and rewrite the claim as gamma_{rect} = gamma_{bot} o gamma_{top} using c = a o b (proof lines 1255-1296).

difficulty_reason: For a commutative diagram of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes whose two squares are cartesian, with f and l as well as g and m Tor independent, the lemma asserts that the base change maps of equation labelled equation-base-change-map for the two squares compose to the base change map of the outer rectangle (statement lines 1237-1253). The proof first notes that g o f and m are then Tor independent, so the statement makes sense, marking that step 'details omitted', and sets a, b, c for the right adjoints of pushforward along f, g and g o f with primed versions for the base changes (proof lines 1255-1266). It writes the arrows gamma_{top}, gamma_{bot} and gamma_{rect} for the two squares and the rectangle as compositions using the canonical maps 1 -> l_* l^* and k^* k_* -> 1 together with the inverses of the base change isomorphisms xi_{top}, xi_{bot}, xi_{rect}, and notes that (g o f)_* = g_* o f_* gives c = a o b and c' = a' o b' (proof lines 1268-1296). The claim is then that gamma_{rect} equals gamma_{bot} o gamma_{top}, which is proved by contemplating a large diagram whose right hand side is the composition and whose left hand side is gamma_{rect}; the quadrilaterals commute by Categories, Lemma labelled categories-lemma-properties-2-cat-cats or the discussion before Categories, Definition labelled categories-definition-horizontal-composition, so it suffices to prove a reduced diagram commutes after inverting xi_{top}, xi_{bot} and xi_{rect} (proof lines 1298-1330). That reduced statement is obtained from a triangle commuting by the same categories lemma, together with two auxiliary quadrilaterals that commute by the cited references and the fact that the composition l_* -> l_* l^* l_* -> l_* is the identity, reducing everything to the identity k o a' o b' -> a o l_* o b -> a o b o m_* being xi_{rect}, which is the statement dual to Cohomology, Remark labelled cohomology-remark-compose-base-change (proof lines 1332-1372). Organising the diagram chase so that only the dual of the known composition of ordinary base change maps remains is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
